items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5
items.author: sfkgtbor
items.summary: According to the sources, Claude Haiku 5.5 is designed for high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks and supports adaptive thinking with the effort parameter, a 1M token context window, and up to 128k output tokens. It uses the same newer tokenizer as later models, resulting in approximately 30% more tokens for the same input text compared to earlier versions. It will join the Claude 5.5 family in the coming weeks. The sources also mention that Sonnet 5.5 is a faster, lower-cost model for everyday tasks, while Sonnet 5.5 scores higher in intelligence and speed compared to Claude 4.5 Haiku. However, the cost per task for Claude 4.5 Haiku is cheaper than Sonnet 5.5.

items.title: Living off-grid: Hundred Rabbits
items.author: Muhammad523
items.summary: The Hundred Rabbits off-grid experience includes challenges such as baby rabbits living in the engine of a Subaru, jackrabbits eating Blue Spruce trees, and Pronghorn Antelope eating deciduous trees. Mice have chewed through wires in the engine and potentially could get into a side by side UTV. Other challenges include mail and package delivery, trash service, getting bulk water, and growing trees when animals chew on them. The longest time spent off-grid was three weeks anchored off Treasure Island in San Francisco. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to some specific questions.

items.title: Show HN: Bigwords.page – Turn any screen into a sign. The URL is the app
items.author: SpeakingOfBrad
items.summary: Bigwords.page is a tool that allows users to turn any screen into a sign by creating full-screen signs, timers, or messages from a link. The service does not require an account or app, and nothing is stored on a server. The link itself serves as the display, which can be shared or bookmarked. The platform offers various use cases, including arrivals signs, quiz timers, café Wi-Fi information, countdowns, QR codes, and images. The message is kept private as it resides in the URL fragment, which browsers do not send to a server.

items.title: GPT‑6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
items.author: joshuawright11
items.summary: GPT-6 is being introduced in ChatGPT and with the ability to construct user interfaces, it starts rolling out to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users today. The rollout will expand to Free and Go tiers starting tomorrow. Intelligent UI allows ChatGPT to answer quickly with fully interactive user interfaces that make everyday answers more visual, making learning complex topics easier and creating tools to solve tasks on the spot. This update applies to the Chat experience in ChatGPT, but the models powering Work and Codex are not changing as part of this release.

items.title: In Vienna and Beijing, the first (thorium) nuclear clocks begin to tick
items.author: gumby
items.summary: In early June, teams in Vienna and Beijing independently developed the first working nuclear clocks, marking a significant achievement in physics. Both teams utilized thorium-229 nuclei in calcium fluoride crystals probed with lasers to achieve this breakthrough. The Vienna team, led by Thorsten Schumm, and the Beijing team, led by Beichen Huang, published their findings on June 3 and June 7, respectively, on the preprint server arXiv. These nuclear clocks, though less accurate than atomic clocks, represent a major step forward in the field, with potential implications for understanding dark matter and other exotic physics scenarios. Neither paper has yet undergone peer review.

items.title: Docker Agent
items.author: saikatsg
items.summary: Docker Agent is an open-source framework for building teams of specialized AI agents that collaborate to solve complex problems. Instead of using a single generalist model, it allows defining agents with specific roles and instructions. Docker Agent is included in Docker Desktop 4.63 and later, and it can be installed via Homebrew. It enables running intelligent AI agents that collaborate without requiring code. Docker Sandboxes natively supports six agent types: Claude Code, Gemini, Codex, Copilot, agent, and Kiro, all of which are experimental.

The convergence of this and Meta's releases in early October 2026 suggests that mathematics has become a showcase field for frontier AI, making it one of the clearest settings for testing whether AI systems can produce genuinely new knowledge. items.title: A new write and space optimized storage engine for MySQL is here
items.author: alexpadula
items.summary: The sources indicate that MyRocks, a new storage engine for MySQL developed by Facebook, integrates RocksDB to provide better compression and reduced write amplification compared to InnoDB. MyRocks is designed for write-intensive and space-intensive workloads. Facebook is in the process of migrating from InnoDB to MyRocks on its main MySQL database tier to use less storage for the same amount of data. However, the sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding the release date or availability of this new storage engine for general MySQL users beyond Facebook's internal use.

items.title: Google Playground: Create and play custom games
items.author: acossta
items.summary: Google Playground is an experimental AI game platform that allows users to create, play, and share custom games without any coding experience. With its conversational interface, users can describe their game ideas through text prompts to create games, customize characters, and tweak environments. The platform is browser-based, making games playable across phones and laptops. It also enables users to share their creations with friends or publish them for the community to play, with plans for future professional-grade tools from Unity Spark.

items.title: Meta and Microsoft take steps to reduce employee usage of Claude AI
items.author: speckx
items.summary: Meta Platforms and Microsoft are taking steps to reduce their workforce's internal reliance on Anthropic's Claude AI models. According to a report by The Information, Microsoft reduced its projected internal spending on Claude by over one-third and plans to end most internal Claude Code licenses by June 30, 2026. Meta saw internal users of Anthropic's Claude Code coding assistant drop from roughly 60,000 to 30,000, and is encouraging staff to use internal options like MetaCode and Muse Code. Both companies are steering developers toward their proprietary AI tools instead of external ones.

items.title: AI-assisted proof of optimal packing for 11 squares
items.author: bluepeter
items.summary: The sources indicate that the optimal packing of 11 squares into a larger square has not been definitively proven. While the sources mention that optimal packings have been proven for several specific numbers of squares, including 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13, 14, 15, 22, 23, 24, 33, 34, and 35, they do not provide a clear answer regarding the optimal packing for exactly 11 squares. The sources do suggest that for n=a^2-a, it is conjectured that the size of the minimum bounding square is a for small n, but this conjecture is violated for n=272 (with a=17). Therefore, the precise optimal packing for 11 squares remains undetermined based on the provided sources.

items.title: Write Like It's 1866: LLMs Relearn Telegraphese
items.author: Theory42
items.summary: A Hacker News thread posted on October 4, 2026, reports that LLMs produce shorter, cheaper outputs when prompted to mimic 1866 telegraph style. The experiment tests whether models can drop modern prose habits and adopt the abbreviated, high-signal format used in paid-by-the-word telegrams. Prompts instruct models to output only essential facts, omit transitions, and use 19th-century abbreviations such as "rec\'d" or "fwd". The Telegraph Test benchmark answers three questions about any model, with the same frozen passage bank, the same anchored questions, and the same deterministic grader every time.

items.title: A font recreated from photographs of classic Commodore 64 keycaps
items.author: sohkamyung
items.summary: A font recreated from photographs of classic Commodore 64 keycaps is available on GitHub by Levente Szabadkai. The font includes cleaned-up shapes and consistent proportions based on the original keycaps. It features uppercase letters, numbers, punctuation, arrows, and £, selected accented letters including Hungarian characters, function-key labels, and all 63 PETSCII graphic front legends. The font is not an exact photo trace but a vector font with inferred frame thickness, curves, and print proportions from the supplied keyboard photograph. The font is uppercase only, as the hardware never sported lowercase letters.

items.title: Mistral Large 4
items.author: Philpax
items.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 49 billion active parameters, making it Mistral's largest and most capable model to date. It ranks among the top five models globally for cybersecurity, scoring 82% on a test to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch it, the highest of any model. It also scores 59.9% on AutomationBench, ahead of other models. The model has a granular Mixture-of-Experts design, activating 52B of 1.05T total parameters, with a 1.6B vision encoder handling images. The cost per 1M tokens is $0.68, input $0.07, cached $2.09, and output $2.09. It is available in a public preview version v26.10 as of October 6, 2026.

items.title: Show HN: Durable Actors – OSS Durable Objects with configurable compute
items.author: thomask1995
items.text:
Hi HN, we're Thomas and Olivier from Terse (https://www.useterse.ai/) We've built Durable Actors, an open-source alternative to Cloudflare's Durable Objects.

A Durable Object/Actor is a tiny server that handles one request at a time and has its own SQLite database. There's exactly one of each in the world and it is addressed by name.

This is the perfect primitive for deploying multiplayer agents. Ea
items.summary: Durable Actors is an open-source alternative to Cloudflare's Durable Objects, designed for concurrent agentic workloads. It is fully open source under the MIT License and includes a helm chart for easy self-hosting. Key features include configurable compute settings such as CPU, RAM, data residency, and idle-timeouts via a decorator. Unlike Cloudflare's Durable Objects, Durable Actors do not require an outer worker and generate a type-safe client that can be integrated into existing tech stacks. The project also promises to soon export SQLite tables via CLI and expose OLTP logs for debugging. Performance metrics include a durable write time of 85.6ms.

items.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
items.author: sasvari
items.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai for their groundbreaking work in asymmetric chemistry, specifically for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. Their work has been revolutionary for chemists developing reactions for the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, flavors, scents, and new materials. The prize was announced on October 7, 2026, at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm. The Nobel committee highlighted the importance of their research in understanding chiral molecules, which exist in mirror-image forms that are similar but not identical.

items.title: Book Recommendations from Hacker News?
items.author: bookofjoe
items.summary: Hacker News users recommend several books for tech and software development, including "Secure by Design," "Designing Data-Intensive Applications," "Building Secure and Reliable Systems," and "Fundamentals of Software Architecture." Sci-fi enthusiasts favor "Murderbot Diaries" and "The Expanse." Other notable mentions are "Careless People" by Sarah Wynn-Williams, "Project Hail Mary" by Andy Weir, and "Dungeon Crawler Carl" by Matt Dinniman. For IT and DevOps, "The Phoenix Project" and "The Unicorn Project" are highly recommended, with "The Phoenix Project" being a good starting point. Additionally, "SQL Performance Explained" by Markus Winand and "The Pragmatic Programmer" by Andrew Hunt and David Thomas are frequently cited as valuable resources.
